findings.title: Unmasking The Gentlemen Ransomware: Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures Revealed
findings.summary_md: Trend Micro documented an August 2025 intrusion by The Gentlemen, then an undocumented group, that began with the compromise of an internet-exposed FortiGate appliance and its administrative account. The attackers killed security tooling with All.exe and ThrottleBlood.sys abusing the signed ThrottleStop.sys driver, then deployed password-protected ransomware domain-wide through the NETLOGON share. Victims spanned 17 countries, with manufacturing, construction, healthcare, and insurance most targeted; encrypted files received .7mtzhh extensions and README-GENTLEMEN.txt ransom notes.

findings.title: Threat Assessment: The Gentlemen Ransomware Group Is Scaling Faster Than Any Other Group on Record
findings.summary_md: Halcyon assesses The Gentlemen split from Qilin after the ArmCorp affiliate's operator hastalamuerte complained on the RAMP forum on 22 July 2025 about roughly $48,000 in unpaid commission, with the first Gentlemen sample appearing on VirusTotal on 17 July 2025. The core team is roughly 20 members, pays affiliates 90% of ransoms, and researchers revealed an inventory of approximately 14,700 already-compromised FortiGate devices plus nearly a thousand brute-forced FortiGate VPN credentials. The report also recounts the 4 May 2026 internal database leak that exposed nine internal accounts, including zeta88.

findings.title: The Gentlemen ransomware: Dissecting a self-propagating Go encryptor
findings.summary_md: Microsoft tracks The Gentlemen as Storm-2697 and dissects the group's self-propagating Go encryptor. This analysis is the source of the Storm-2697 identifier used in later vendor reporting on the group.

findings.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group The Gentlemen?
findings.summary_md: Brian Krebs published evidence on the identity of hastalamuerte, founder and administrator of The Gentlemen, whom Group-IB describes as a disgruntled former Qilin affiliate. The reporting builds on the group's May 2026 internal data leak.

findings.title: Killing me gently: Inside Gentlemen's EDR killer framework
findings.summary_md: ESET details GentleKiller, The Gentlemen's operator-maintained EDR-killer framework with at least eight variants abusing vulnerable or malicious drivers, staged from a GentlemenCollection directory alongside the third-party killers HexKiller, ThrottleBlood, and HavocKiller. GentleKiller targets more than 400 processes across 48 security products, and ESET observes the gang's victimology is globally distributed with no strong US focus.

findings.title: The Gentlemen RaaS
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's Securelist published technical analysis of The Gentlemen RaaS, documenting ransomware variants written in C and Go and a custom Go-based backdoor used by the group. Unit 42's July 2026 report cites this write-up for the group's encryption tooling.

findings.title: Not Very Gentlemanly: Analyzing a Zero-Day Exploit Used by The Gentlemen Ransomware to Disable Targets' EDRs
findings.summary_md: Expel analyzed a zero-day exploit used by The Gentlemen ransomware to disable targets' EDR products. Unit 42 cites this post as the source for the group's suspected zero-day defense evasion.
